text:
Sebastian Aho took the Hurricanes to Finland for the Global Series and scored in his home country, a trip North State Journal's Cory Lavalette called "unreal" for him and Juuso Valimaki. He had two goals against Seattle in Helsinki, part of a four-game point streak (3 goals, 5 assists).

He has 29 points in 21 games, and he's winning faceoffs at the best rate of his career, which he described to Lavalette as "kind of like playing chess a little bit."

Some of the scoring is borrowed. He's shooting 20.7% against an expected range around 14.6%, and Carolina has scored 7.4 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice. Our season range runs from 81 to 107 points, wide because a cooling finish is likely.

Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.9 wins above replacement last season with a strong play-driving number (94th percentile among forwards), with the note that his teammates are strong too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags one habit: he shoots a lot, but fewer of his attempts come from the slot than the volume suggests. Watch whether he gets inside.
headline: Aho went home and played like it
